item.title: Malta airport hit by 3.7 million cyberattack attempts in six months
item.description: Malta International Airport was targeted by more than 3.7 million attempted cyber-attacks in the first six months of the year, its head of IT management said. Phishing emails aimed at harvesting login details were described as the airport's biggest threat, with the head of IT noting that attackers are using AI to craft more targeted, correctly punctuated messages that mimic genuine communication styles. The disclosure was made in the Malta Stock Exchange plc Business Review.

The disclosure was made in the Malta Stock Exchange plc Business Review.

Sources: Times of Malta, The Business Picture, Lovin Malta

item.title: Man accused of blackmailing girls granted bail
item.description: Gian-Luke Gambin, 27, from Victoria, Gozo, was granted bail subject to electronic monitoring, nearly six months after his 8 June arraignment. He faces 56 criminal charges including sexual exploitation and corruption of minors, blackmail and the production of indecent material, alleged to have been carried out through fake social media profiles. Bail was ordered against a EUR10,000 deposit and a EUR40,000 personal guarantee.

item.title: Auditors flag persistent failings in councils
item.description: Five local councils face uncertainty over meeting their financial obligations, a National Audit Office report tabled in parliament shows. Attard, Dingli, Kalkara, Victoria and Zebbug may need extra income and better cash-flow management, while auditors flagged persistent shortcomings in accounting, procurement and administrative practice.

Sources: Times of Malta

item.title: 68% of Gozitans expect religious life to decline
item.description: A survey commissioned by the Diocese of Gozo, conducted among more than 400 people in summer 2026, found that 68% believe religious life on the island will decline over the next decade, despite 70.6% of respondents saying they attend Sunday Mass regularly and a further 17.7% attending frequently.

item.title: Heritage NGOs urge PA to refuse Siggiewi reservoir plan
item.description: The Archaeological Society Malta and Din l-Art Helwa are urging the Planning Authority to refuse an application to excavate a water reservoir and reinstate a roof over a pre-1967 structure at Ghar il-Kbir, Siggiewi, next to a scheduled cave site. The application, PA/08170/25, is filed by Simon Mizzi.

item.title: MEP David Casa secures ESF mandate in Parliament
item.description: MEPs voted overwhelmingly in favour of the negotiating mandate for the post-2027 European Social Fund secured by David Casa, the EPP said, defeating a far-right objection to the text. Casa will enter negotiations with national governments in Council early next year before the new ESF measures are rolled out.

item.title: Nine in ten students use AI weekly, many feel unprepared
item.description: Two Malta Further and Higher Education Authority surveys found 91.5% of students use artificial intelligence weekly for learning, study and research, yet half say they feel unprepared to use it well. The reports, drawn from March and May, say AI adoption is outpacing institutional preparedness, identifying gaps in training, academic integrity and institutional policy.

Sources: Times of Malta, Newsbook

item.title: PN calls for stronger action on violence against women
item.description: Marking the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, the Nationalist Party called for greater investment in prevention, education grounded in respect and equality, and stronger support services for victims, including attention to emerging forms of abuse such as digital violence. A national campaign against domestic violence was also launched on Wednesday.

item.title: EU medicines rules approved to widen Malta's supplier base
item.description: The European Parliament approved sweeping reforms to EU pharmaceutical legislation that will let Malta source medicines from a broader range of European suppliers. From 2028, small states will be able to require companies to supply specific medicines locally, with three years to comply or risk losing market exclusivity in Malta. Amendments proposed by MEP Peter Agius also aim to ease recurring shortages and, by increasing competition, potentially lower prices.

item.title: Maltas business community grew by around 4,000 companies last year
item.description: Malta had just over 65,700 active businesses last year, up from just under 61,800 a year earlier, according to provisional National Statistics Office figures published on Wednesday. Those businesses accounted for almost 290,000 jobs, an increase of around 5% on the previous year. Transport and storage, financial and insurance businesses registered the strongest proportional growth at around 12%, while 94% of active enterprises still employed fewer than 10 people each.

item.title: Active Maltese businesses up by nearly 4,000 in 2025
item.description: Provisional NSO figures show Malta had 65,732 active enterprises at end-2025, up 6.4% on the previous year and nearly 4,000 more than a year earlier. The firms sustained 289,943 jobs, an increase of about 5%, with transport, financial services and real estate showing the strongest proportional growth. About 94% of active enterprises employed fewer than ten people.

item.title: Police Commissioner refers ex-inspector claims to complaints board
item.description: Police Commissioner Angelo Gafa has asked the Independent Police Complaints Board to examine claims by a former inspector that his 2020 report on tampered import paperwork for second-hand vehicles was ignored. Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield confirmed the referral on Wednesday. The former inspector, Jeffrey Scicluna Briffa, testified on Tuesday that documents authorising the release of imported vehicles were in some cases stamped before the required inspections were carried out. The allegations centre on an odometer-tampering racket involving Japanese-imported cars, first exposed in 2022, in which several police officers were charged and five were acquitted earlier this year.

item.title: KSU criticises threat to withhold university exam results
item.description: The University of Maltas student council said students must not be used as bargaining tools in the dispute over unpaid lecturer salaries. KSU said in a Facebook post on Wednesday that it was concerned examination results could be withheld, noting that assurances to the contrary were given last year. The move follows a directive from the University of Malta Academic Staff Association instructing academics not to publish results until guarantees are provided over outstanding payments under a new collective agreement. The dispute concerns salary arrears, with no guarantee the full amounts will be paid by 28 January 2027.

item.title: European Commission warns Malta's budget risks breaching EU spending limits
item.description: The European Commission said Malta's draft budgetary plan is at risk of material non-compliance with the EU's maximum net expenditure growth limit, singling out energy tariff subsidies as a key factor. Net expenditure is projected to rise 10.2% in 2026, well above the 5.8% ceiling recommended by the EU Council, and by 6.3% in 2027. The Commission noted the fiscal cost of untargeted energy subsidies is set to climb from 0.9% of GDP in 2025 to around 1.8% in 2026, and called on Malta to act. The draft plan was submitted on 15 October, 11 days before Budget day.

item.title: Government to set up dedicated agency for Malta in Motion in 2027
item.description: Transport Minister Chris Bonett told Parliament that a dedicated agency would be established in 2027 to coordinate the Malta in Motion masterplan, which combines buses, ferries, walking, cycling, parking and a proposed rail service. He said the government is exploring larger car parks on town outskirts linked to circular bus routes, with Marsaskala flagged as a first test case, and that national parking and walking strategies are due in 2027. Bonett also said the bus network needs improvement and that more circular routes are planned for Rabat, Pembroke and the Three Cities.

item.title: 55 women murdered since 1970, 65% by current or former partners
item.description: The Malta Observatory on Femicide said at least 55 women have been killed in Malta since 1970, with 36 of the cases (65%) involving a current or former intimate partner. Twenty killings occurred during an ongoing abusive relationship and 16 in the context of an actual or planned separation. The Observatory issued its appeal ahead of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, recalling the recent murders of Charlotte Zammit, Miriam Azzopardi and Mary Grace Cassar.

item.title: Another mobile phone found in prison cell during night raid
item.description: A mobile phone was found in a prison cell on Tuesday evening, a month after three prisoners were similarly found in possession of phones. Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield said the raid was carried out by prison officers and police as part of an investigation running several weeks. The three prisoners previously caught with phones include George Degiorgio and Robert Agius, convicted over the killing of journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia, and Damiano Torrisi; Agius and Torrisi were suspected of using phones to plot a murder. Bedingfield said possession of phones in prison is to be made a crime.

item.title: University academics to withhold exam marks over unpaid arrears
item.description: The University of Malta Academic Staff Association has told members not to publish examination or assignment results until arrears owed under their collective agreement are paid in full, saying no guarantee was given that the money would be paid with the January paycheque. The union declared an industrial dispute on 5 November after November's paycheque omitted arrears stemming from a May collective agreement, approved by 95% of members, that runs to 2029. Professors are estimated to be owed between €25,000 and €30,000, with lower bands due between €10,000 and €20,000.

item.title: Controversial Rahal Ġdid UCA development set to be refused
item.description: The Planning Authority is expected to refuse application PA/7261/26, which proposes replacing two townhouses on Triq l-Arkata near the 17th-century parish church of St Ubaldeska, a Grade 1 scheduled property. The proposal, lodged by G3 Estates Ltd, would build a complex with 12 underground parking spaces, two maisonettes, 20 apartments and a pool house. The authority received over 600 individual objections by the 20 November deadline, including one organised by the parish signed by 236 people, and the case officer has entered a negative recommendation in his report.

item.title: Man, 20, charged with raping 18-year-old on St Julian's rocky beach
item.description: A 20-year-old man was charged in court with raping an 18-year-old woman at the rocky beach in San Ġiljan, it emerged on Wednesday. The accused, Toby Jude Dixon Raphael, a Malta-born holder of a British passport who works in iGaming, was identified and arrested on Monday. The prosecution told the court this was the second such charge against him in the past 18 months and asked for his name to be published so other victims may come forward; the court ordered publication, and the defence asked for bail, which was opposed.

item.title: Swimmer airlifted to safety from Coral Lagoon at Mellieħa
item.description: A swimmer was airlifted to safety on Tuesday afternoon after she got into difficulty at the Coral Lagoon near l-Aħrax in Mellieħa and could not climb out. The Armed Forces of Malta said a helicopter hoisted her out of the area, with Civil Protection Department rescuers, an ambulance crew and Malta Red Cross first aiders also on scene. The Coral Lagoon is a natural collapsed sea cave connected to the open sea, popular for kayaking, snorkelling, paddleboarding and photography.

item.title: Malta Polo Club petitions government over Marsa grounds
item.description: Malta Polo Club has launched a petition calling on the government to return its historic grounds in Marsa, after the club was left without its main pitch and clubhouse following redevelopment works. Around 8,500 spectators watched the Cawnpore Cup on 21 June 2025 before the club handed over the grounds for redevelopment and packed up its clubhouse; the pitch has still not been returned and the clubhouse has since been demolished. The club is asking for the polo ground to be removed from the wider Marsa racecourse concession and a direct long-term emphyteutic lease granted instead.

item.title: Nine in ten students use AI for study every week, survey finds
item.description: More than nine in ten further and higher education students use artificial intelligence for learning, study or research in a typical week, but only around one in four say their curriculum covers AI topics relevant to their field. The findings come from two Malta Further and Higher Education Authority surveys run in March and April 2026, covering 1,306 students and 232 education providers. Some 56% of students said they do not feel sufficiently trained in AI for the future job market, with both educators and students calling for standardised national direction.

item.title: Call it what it is: national campaign launched for 16 days of activism against domestic violence
item.description: A national campaign under the theme Call it what it is was launched on Wednesday to mark the 16 Days of Activism against domestic violence. Social Policy and Family Minister Michael Falzon said prevention, awareness, access to justice and stronger support services are essential so victims feel safe seeking help. Equality and Civil Rights Minister Rosianne Cutajar said the campaign targets the root causes of gender-based violence, including harmful gender stereotypes, sexism and gender inequalities.

item.title: Robert Agius Tal-Maksar found with another mobile phone in prison cell
item.description: Robert Agius, known as Ta Maksar, was the inmate found with a mobile phone during a Tuesday evening raid on his cell at the Corradino Correctional Facility, Times of Malta can confirm. It is the second time in just over a month that Agius has been caught with a phone, having been among three inmates found with phones last month. He is serving a life sentence for supplying the bomb that killed investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia, and was being questioned by police on Wednesday morning. How the phones reached the prison remains unclear.

item.title: Four HSBC Malta investment funds hit record highs
item.description: Four funds managed by HSBC Global Asset Managements Malta team reached record unit prices this year, with two posting returns of 9% or more in the first ten months. The Equity Growth Fund returned 12.6% between January and October, reaching a record EUR 528, while the Maltese Assets Fund returned 9% to a record EUR 698. The Malta Bond Fund hit EUR 700 in August and the International Bond Fund EUR 485 in July. By end-October the team managed and distributed more than EUR 1 billion in assets, up 13.8% year on year.

item.title: Court hears mother say Tristan B conned family out of daughters cremation fund
item.description: A mother who lost her child in 2024 told a court on Wednesday that singer Tristan B took advantage of her familys vulnerability and convinced them to lend him EUR 5,500 from their daughters cremation fund. The testimony was given during the compilation of evidence against Emanuel Balzan, better known by his stage name, who is charged with defrauding eight individuals and forging the signatures of well-known Maltese singers and businesses to validate fictitious projects. The witness said she found the singer on Facebook after her daughters death and asked him to sing at a mass.

item.title: BirdLife calls for end to finch trapping after second EU warning
item.description: BirdLife Malta has called on the government to withdraw the finch trapping derogation after the European Commission issued a second warning over its continued authorisation under the guise of scientific research. In a reasoned opinion dated 19 November, the Commission said the derogation did not meet the requirements of genuine scientific research and allowed trapping for recreational purposes, and that Malta had not shown there were no satisfactory alternatives. The Commission has given Malta two months to address the issues before considering further legal action.

item.title: Malta secures cruising privileges in the United States
item.description: The United States has extended reciprocal cruising privileges to Maltese-flagged pleasure yachts, a significant milestone for Maltas maritime and yachting sector. US Customs and Border Protection formally amended its regulations on 29 October 2026 to add Malta to the list of countries whose pleasure vessels may be issued cruising licences in the US. Under the regime, qualifying foreign-flagged yachts used exclusively for pleasure can benefit from simplified customs formalities when navigating between US ports, strengthening the competitiveness of the Maltese flag.

item.title: Public Works objects to two Qormi rezoning applications over flood risk
item.description: The Public Works Department has objected to two separate Qormi applications seeking to rezone land for residential development, warning they could increase flood risks for neighbouring properties and undermine future flood mitigation. Both objections, dated 13 November, were signed by Mario Ellul, director of the PWD's Coastal and Stormwater Directorate. The first concerns a 4,297 sq m vacant site on Triq Amleto Spiteri proposed for five-storey residential blocks, while the second covers a smaller 360 sq m partly residential site near Triq l-Għoxrin ta' Jannar.
item.content:encoded:
The Public Works Department has objected to two separate Qormi applications seeking to rezone land for residential development, warning they could increase flood risks for neighbouring properties and undermine future flood mitigation. Both objections, dated 13 November, were signed by Mario Ellul, director of the PWD's Coastal and Stormwater Directorate. The first concerns a 4,297 sq m vacant site on Triq Amleto Spiteri proposed for five-storey residential blocks, while the second covers a smaller 360 sq m partly residential site near Triq l-Għoxrin ta' Jannar.

Sources: MaltaToday
